sections.name: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR

items.label: Required Upper-Division
items.notes:
- If applying to the BS/MS Materials program, third year students must take the MATRL 100A in Fall, MATRL 100B in Winter, and MATRL 100C in Spring.
- Students may only count one of MATRL 101 OR MATRL 100C toward the major.

items.label: Technical Elective requirement
items.description:
Prior approval of the student’s technical electives must be obtained from the undergraduate adviser.
At least 9 of the 15 units must be in the following departments in the College of Engineering: CH E, ECE, MATRL, ME
items.notes: Three units maximum from CH E 196 and CH E 198 combined; only for students with GPA of 3.0 or higher.

sections.notes: To satisfy major requirements, courses taken inside or outside the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, must be taken for a letter grade.

nodes.title: Introduction to Chemical Engineering Design
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Registration is restricted to Chemical Engineering majors only for passes 1 & 2.

requires.text: Registration is restricted to Chemical Engineering majors only

nodes.description: Introduction to the design and analysis of processes involving chemical change in the context of chemical and biomolecular engineering. Students learn mathematical, empirical, and conceptual strategies to analyze chemical processes to assess product quality, economics, safety, and environmental issues. Focus topics include an overview of chemical and biomolecular engineering, evaluating and analyzing data, flowsheets, material and energy balances, economics, and unit operations.

nodes.title: Material and Energy Balances
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 5 (may be taken concurrently); Chemistry 1A-B or 3A-B; Mathematics 2A or 3A, Mathematics 2B or 3B and Mathematics 4A or 4AI
nodes.description: Elementary principles and problem solving skills required for quantitative analysis of chemical processes. Topics to be covered include macroscopic material and energy balances, reaction stoichiometry, elementary thermodynamics, and phase equilibria associated with chemical engineering processes and unit operations.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement

nodes.title: Introduction to Biological Processing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10
nodes.description: Familiarizes engineering students with biological processing and production at multiple scales. Chemical engineering principles will be infused with key biological concepts, including an introduction to biochemistry, cell biology, and molecular biology.

nodes.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 5; Chemical Engineering 10; Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Chemistry 1C or 3C.
nodes.description: Use of the laws of thermodynamics to analyze processes encountered in engineering practice, including cycles and flows. Equations-of-state for describing properties of fluids and mixtures. Applications, including engines, turbines, refrigeration and power plant cycles, phase equilibria, and chemical-reaction equilibria.

nodes.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4B or 4BI.
nodes.description: Extension of Chemical Engineering 110A to cover mixtures and multiphase equilibrium. Liquid-vapor separations calculations are emphasized. Introduction to equations of state for mixtures.

nodes.title: Technical Communication of Chemical Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A
nodes.description: Provides an introduction to technical communication in the form of writing reports and oral presentations. Emphasis placed on how to analyze and present data; critical thinking; organization, logic and constructing a technical narrative; literature searching and citations for written reports; and how to give oral presentations. Includes various lectures on technical communication, individual and group assignments, and peer-review exercises.

nodes.title: Transport Processes
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10 with a minimum grade of C- (may be taken concurrently); Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI and Mathematics 6B.
nodes.description: Introductory course in conceptual understanding and mathematical analysis of problems in fluid dynamics of relevance to Chemical Engineering. Emphasis is placed on performing microscopic and macroscopic mathematical analysis to understand fluid motion in response to forces.

nodes.title: Transport Processes
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10 with minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110A with minimum grade of C- (may be taken concurrently); Chemical Engineering 120A.
nodes.description: Introductory course in the mathematical analysis of conductive, convective and radiative heat transfer with practical applications to design of heat exchange equipment and use.

nodes.title: Transport Processes
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10 with a minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110A with minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110B (may be taken concurrently) and Chemical Engineering 120B.
nodes.description: Introductory course in the fundamentals of mass transfer with applications to the design of mass transfer equipment.

nodes.title: Colloids and Biosurfaces
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.description: Basic forces and interactions between atoms, molecules, small particles and extended surfaces. Special features and interactions associated with (soft) biological molecules, biomaterials and surfaces: lipids, proteins, fibrous molecules (DNA), biological membranes, hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions, bio-specific and non-equilibrium interactions.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement

nodes.title: Non-Newtonian Fluids, Soft Materials and Chemical Products
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 120C (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Overview of soft materials (suspensions, gels, polymers, surfactants, emulsions, powders and granules) that arise in diverse industries, including consumer products, foods, advanced materials, biotechnology, and mineral and energy production. Influence of non-Newtonian rheology (shear-thickening and thinning, viscoelasticity, extension-thickening, yield stresses, normal stress differences, and metastability) upon handling, processing, production, and performance of chemical products. Strategies to design chemical products that meet performance targets, and to scale-up production. Real-world case studies and classroom demonstrations.

nodes.title: Separation Processes
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10, and 110A-B; open to Engineering majors only.
nodes.description: Basic principles and design techniques of equilibrium-stage separation processes. Emphasis is placed on binary distillation, liquid-liquid extraction, and multicomponent distillation.

nodes.title: Analytical Methods in Chemical Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI. Space may be limited, and registration priority will be given to Chemical Engineering majors.
nodes.description: Develop analytical tools to solve elementary partial differential equations and boundary value problems. Separation of variables, Laplace transforms, Sturm-Liouville theory, generalized Fourier analysis, and computer math tools.

nodes.title: Computational Methods in Chemical Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI; Mathematics 6B and Engineering 3.
nodes.description: Numerical methods for solution of linear and nonlinear algebraic equations, optimization, interpolation, numerical integration and differentiation, initial-value problems in ordinary and partial differential equations, and boundary-value problems. Emphasis on computational tools for chemical engineering applications.

nodes.title: Statistical Methods in Chemical Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI and Mathematics 6B.
nodes.description: Probability concepts and distributions, random variables, error analysis, point estimation and confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, development of empirical chemical engineering models using regression techniques, design of experiments, process monitoring based on statistical quality control techniques.

nodes.title: Chemical Reaction Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10 with minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110A with a minimum grade of C-; Chemical Engineering 110B (may be taken concurrently). Chemical Engineering 120A-B.
nodes.description: Fundamentals of chemical reaction engineering with emphasis on kinetics of homogenous and heterogeneous reacting systems. A microkinetic understanding of reaction rates is linked to reactor design, chemical conversion, and selectivity. Batch and continuous reactor designs with and without catalysts are examined.

nodes.title: Chemical Reaction Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A-B, 120A-B and 140A.
nodes.description: Thermodynamics, kinetics, mass and energy transport considerations associated with complex homogeneous and heterogeneous reacting systems. Catalysts and catalytic reaction rates and mechanisms. Adsorption and reaction at solid surfaces, including effects of diffusion in porous materials. Chemical reactors using heterogeneous catalysts.

nodes.title: The Science and Engineering of Energy Conversion
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: ChE 110A (or equivalent thermodynamics) and ChE 140A (or equivalent chemical kinetics); OR Chem 112A-B-C or Chem 113A-B-C; OR consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Framework for understanding the energy supply issues facing society with a focus on the science, engineering, and economic principles of the major alternatives. Emphasis is on the physical and chemical fundamentals of energy conversion technologies.

nodes.title: Heterogeneous Catalysis
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 140A and B or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Concepts and definitions. Applications of heterogeneous catalysis. Performance metrics. Analysis of surface reaction mechanisms and complex reaction networks. Structure-function relationships for supported metal and zeolite catalysts. Synthesis and characterization of heterogeneous catalysts.

nodes.title: Process Dynamics and Control
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 120A-B-C and 140A.
nodes.description: Development of theoretical and empirical models for chemical and physical processes, dynamic behavior of processes, transfer function and block diagram representation, process instrumentation, control system design and analysis, stability analysis, computer simulation of controlled processes.

nodes.title: Advanced Process Control
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 152A.
nodes.description: The theory, design, and experimental application of advanced process control strategies including feedforward control, cascade control, enhanced single-loop strategies, and model predictive control. Analysis of multi-loop control systems. Introduction to on-line optimization.

nodes.title: Engineering Approaches to Systems Biology
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 170 or Chemical Engineering 107; Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI and Mathematics 6B.
nodes.description: Applications of engineering tools and methods to solve problems in systems biology. Emphasis is placed on integrative approaches that address multi_scale and multi-rate phenomena in biological regulation. Modeling, optimization, and sensitivity analysis tools are introduced.

nodes.title: Introduction to Polymer Science
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A or Chemistry 113A or equivalent.
nodes.description: Introductory course covering synthesis, characterization, structure, and mechanical properties of polymers. The course is taught from a materials perspective and includes polymer thermodynamics, chain architecture, measurement and control of molecular weight as well as crystallization and glass transitions.

nodes.title: Mechatronics and Instrumentation for Chemical Engineers
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Engineering 3 and Chemical Engineering 110A and B, or consent of instructor
nodes.description: Introduction to electromechanical systems and instrumentation used in Chemical Engineering. Fundamentals of transducers, sensors and actuators; interfacing and controlling hardware with software (Labview & Matlab programming); analog and digital circuits; hands-on electrical and mechanical design, prototyping, and construction. Students produce a final computer-controlled electromechanical project of their own design, or in conjunction with a ChE-faculty research laboratory.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement

nodes.title: Omics-enabled Biotechnology
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 170 or Chemical Engineering 107 or MCDB 1A and consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Integrates genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and proteomic approaches to quantify and understand intricate biological systems. Complementary bioinformatics approaches to curate the large datasets associated with these experiments will also be discussed. Recent examples from the literature will reinforce core concepts, ranging from applications to human health to the environment. By the end of the course, students should be able to design an integrated experiment that capitalizes on these omics-based approaches to enhance the scope of their research.

nodes.title: Biocircuit Design for Engineers
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 10, Chemical Engineering 107 or equivalent or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Introduction to fundamental principles underlying synthetic biology with an emphasis on mathematical modeling of gene regulation using ordinary differential equations and mass action kinetics. Students are introduced to foundational concepts in molecular and cellular engineering, synthetic biology, quantitative modeling of various genetic circuits, as well as cutting edge applications of innovative molecular biotechnologies such as cancer immunotherapy and cell-based diagnostics. Students will also learn to design and predict the functional outcomes of synthetic gene circuits and review primary literature in the field. At the end of this course, students are expected to develop a quantitative understanding of genetic circuit design.

nodes.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A and 120A-B.
nodes.description: Experiments in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, mass transfer, and chemical processing. Analysis of results, and preparation of reports.

nodes.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 120C, 128, 140A and 152A.
nodes.description: Experiments in mass transfer, reactor kinetics, process control, and chemical and biochemical processing. Analysis of results, and preparation of reports.

nodes.title: Design of Chemical Processes
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A-B, 120A-B-C, 128, 132B, 140A-B, and 152A.
nodes.description: Applications of chemical engineering principles to reactor and plant design. Conceptual design of chemical processes. Flowsheeting methods. Engineering cost principles and economic aspects.

nodes.title: Design of Chemical Processes
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 184A.
nodes.description: The solution to comprehensive plant design problems. Use of computer process simulators. Optimization of plant design, investment and operations.

nodes.title: Undergraduate Research
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing, completion of 2 upper-division courses in Chemical Engineering; consent of the instructor.

items.text: completion of 2 upper-division courses in Chemical Engineering

nodes.description: Research opportunities for undergraduate students. Students are expected to give regular oral presentations, actively participate in a weekly seminar, and prepare at least one written report on their research.

nodes.title: Independent Studies in Chemical Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Chemical Engineering.

items.text: completion of 2 upper-division courses in Chemical Engineering

nodes.description: Directed individual studies.

nodes.title: General Chemistry
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory).

nodes.title: General Chemistry
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: kinetics; intermolecular forces, liquids and solids; properties of solutions; transition metals and coordination complexes; organic chemistry and polymers; nuclear chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
nodes.description: The sequence of topics will be similar to that in Chemistry 1A. Calculus will be used as needed, at the level of the concurrent Mathematics 3A course.

nodes.title: General Chemistry Lab (Part A)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A, or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-. Concurrent enrollment, or a grade of C- or higher in CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B.
nodes.description: Qualitative and quantitative measurements to develop laboratory techniques and demonstrate the basic concepts of stoichiometry, gas laws, atomic spectroscopy, chemical equilibrium, and acid-base chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 2A or CHEM 1A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Thermodynamics (first and second law), electrochemistry, chemical kinetics, atomic and molecular structure, and chemical bonding.

nodes.title: General Chemistry Laboratory (Part B)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-. Concurrent enrollment, or a grade of C- or higher in CHEM 1C, CHEM 2C, or CHEM 3C. CHEM 2AL (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Qualitative and quantitative measurements to develop laboratory techniques and demonstrate the basic concepts of buffers, thermochemistry, electrochemistry, kinetics, and colligative properties.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 2B or CHEM 1B or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Structure and dynamics of the elements and their compounds. Aspects of technology and environmental problems.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: None
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory). First quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A, or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry. Second quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: kinetics; intermolecular forces, liquids and solids; properties of solutions; transition metals and coordination complexes; organic chemistry and polymers; nuclear chemistry. Third quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: Laboratory Methods of Organic Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1AL or 2AC, 1BL or 2BC, and 1CL or 2CC, or Chemistry 2AL and 2BL; 109A or 109AH or 130A with a minimum grade of a C-; and Chemistry 109B or 109BH or 130B (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Distillation, crystallization, extraction, determination of physical properties, spectroscopy, and instrumental methods in organic chemistry.

nodes.title: Laboratory Methods of Organic Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 6AL and 109A or 109AH or 130A with a minimum grade of C-; and Chemistry 130B (can be taken concurrently) or Chemistry 109B or 109BH.
nodes.description: Distillation, crystallization, extraction, determination of physical properties, organic synthesis, instrumental methods in organic chemistry.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C or 2C or 3C with a minimum grade of C-; or Chemistry 1B or 2B or 3B with a minimum grade of B-.
nodes.description: Introduction to organic chemistry. Topics include acid/base chemistry, conformational analysis, stereoisomers, thermodynamics and kinetics, aromaticity and resonance, and multistep synthesis as well as the nomenclature, structure, reactivity, and mechanisms of alkenes, alkynes, and alkyl halides. Reaction mechanisms include electrophilic addition, substitution, and elimination reactions.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry (H)
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1B/2B or 1C/2C with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Structure, nomenclature, stereochemistry, and reactivity of organic molecules. Suitable for undergraduates requiring strong understanding of organic chemistry and possessing strong background in science, such as honors students, majors in chemistry, biochemistry-chem, chemical engineering, etc. This course cannot be repeated.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 130A, 109A or 109AH with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis, and nomenclature of organic molecules including alcohols, radicals, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids and carboxylic acid derivatives, and aromatic rings. Other topics include organometallic compounds and reactions at the alpha carbon.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry (H)
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 109A with a minimum grade of B+ or Chemistry 109AH with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Structure, nomenclature, stereochemistry, and reactivity of organic molecules. Suitable for undergraduates requiring strong understanding of organic chemistry and possessing strong background in science, such as honors students, majors in chemistry, biochemistry-chem, chemical engineering, etc. This course cannot be repeated.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 130B or 109B or 109BH with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Structure, reactivity and synthesis of organic molecules including nomenclature, reaction mechanisms, and stereochemistry. Topics include organometallics, polymers, carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids, coenzymes and their mechanisms.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry (H)
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 109B with a minimum grade of B+ or Chemistry 109BH with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis, nomenclature, and spectroscopic identification of the principal classes of organic compounds as well as organometallics, amino acids, proteins, and carbohydrates. This course is intended for chemistry majors and others requiring a strong basis in organic chemistry.

nodes.title: Biophysical Chemistry
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C or 2C or 3C; and, Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B, and 6A; and, Physics 7A-B-C-L, or, Physics 1, 2, 3, 3L, 4, and 4L, or, Physics 6A-AL-B-BL-C-CL; Chemistry 142A, Chem W 142A or MCDB 108A (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Laws of thermodynamics, chemical equilibria and ligand binding, phase equilibria, electrochemistry, nonelectrolyte solutions, applications to biochemical problems.

nodes.title: Biophysical Chemistry
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 112A; Chemistry 142A or Chemistry W 142A or MCDB 108A; Chemistry 142B or MCDB 108B (may be taken concurrently); Math 4A.
nodes.description: Forces influencing macromolecular conformation, microscopy and diffraction methods, quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics.

nodes.title: Biophysical Chemistry
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 112B; Chemistry 142B or MCDB 108B; Chemistry 142C or MCDB 108C (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Biological spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance, mass transport dynamics in solution, chemical and biochemical kinetics.

nodes.title: Physical Chemistry
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C or 2C; and, Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B, and 6A; and, Physics 7A-B-C-L, or, Physics 1-2-3-3L-4-4L, or, Physics 6A-AL-B-BL-C-CL.
nodes.description: Chemical thermodynamics: laws of thermodynamics, phase equilibria, chemical equilibria, equations of state.

nodes.title: Physical Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 113A or Chemical Engineering 110A-B; Math 4A.
nodes.description: Quantum theory and spectroscopy: introduction to quantum mechanics; symmetry, molecular structure, and spectroscopy.

nodes.title: Physical Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 113B.
nodes.description: Kinetic theory of gases, chemical kinetics, statistical mechanics, photochemistry.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B, and Chemistry 113A-B-C or Chemistry 112A-B-C.
nodes.description: Introduction to quantum mechanics-postulatory approach; particle in box, on ring, harmonic oscillator; linear operator theory, matrix algebra; hydrogen atom; perturbation theory, variation theory; applications.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 115A
nodes.description: Molecular orbital theory and valence bond theory; Huckel theory (secular eqn.) applications to conjugated systems, electronic spectra, and term symbols; introduction to infrared, Raman, and microwave spectroscopy.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 115A.
nodes.description: Introduction to NMR, EPR, group theory; and applications.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Environmental Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B.
nodes.description: Study of Earth's biogeochemical cycles with respect to carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur. Introduction to the science of climate change, including effects of global warming on terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. Environmental impacts of fossil fuel and biofuel technologies. Chemistry of the atmosphere, hydrosphere, and lithosphere, with emphasis on ozone depletion, photochemical smog, acid rain, global ocean acidification, soil and groundwater contamination, and environmental costs of industrialized agriculture.

nodes.title: Computation Chemistry and Molecular Modeling
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 109A-B.
nodes.description: Introduction to computational chemistry and molecular modeling. Application of molecular mechanics, quantum mechanics and computer graphical interfaces to problems in chemistry, biochemistry, drug design and pharmacology.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry for Majors
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C or 2C or 3C with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Introduction to organic chemistry. Topics include acid/base chemistry, conformational analysis, stereoisomers, thermodynamics and kinetics, aromaticity and resonance, and multistep synthesis as well as the nomenclature, structure, reactivity, and mechanisms of alkenes, alkynes, and alkyl halides. Reaction mechanisms include electrophilic addition, substitution, and elimination reactions. This course is intended for chemistry majors and others requiring a strong basis in organic chemistry.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry for Majors
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 130A, 109A or 109AH with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis, and nomenclature of organic molecules including alcohols, radicals, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids and carboxylic acid derivatives, and aromatic rings. Other topics include organometallic compounds and reactions at the alpha carbon. This course is intended for chemistry majors and others requiring a strong basis in organic chemistry.

nodes.title: Biochemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 107A-B-C or 109A or 109AH-109B or 109BH-109C or 109CH or W 109C
nodes.description: Macromolecules of biological importance. A survey of the physical and chemical properties of proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates. Methods of preparation, chemical synthesis, degradation, and characterization of biomolecules.

nodes.title: Biochemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chem 142A or Chem W 142A.
nodes.description: Chemical aspects of intermediary metabolism. The chemistry and elementary dynamic properties of enzymes; study of enzyme active sites; characterization of metabolic pathways and methods of examining cellular regulation.

nodes.title: Biochemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 142B.
nodes.description: Macromolecular biosynthesis and specialized cellular processes. A survey of nucleic acid and protein biosynthesis, characterization of lipids and membranes; function of membranes in transport, energy transduction, and cellular control; mechanisms of muscle contraction and cell motility.

nodes.title: Computational Biochemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 113A-B or Chemistry 112A-B; and, Chemistry 142A or Chem W142A or MCDB 108A.
nodes.description: Introduction to molecular modeling and molecular dynamics. Discussion of practical considerations of energy minimization, solvent modeling, structure-based drug design. Practical computer graphics experience.

nodes.title: Astrobiology and the Origins of Life
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 142A or Chem W142A or MCDB 108A.
nodes.description: Discusses the origins and evolution of the solar system and the earth, the origins and evolution of life on earth, and the possibilities for life elsewhere in the cosmos, all from the perspective of contemporary, terrain biochemistry.

nodes.title: Analytical Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B-C or 2A-B-C.
nodes.description: Principles of analytical chemistry including classical techniques, spectrophotochemistry, electroanalytical techniques, and separation processes.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 130B or 109B or 109BH with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: An online class that studies the structure, reactivity, mechanisms, synthesis and nomenclature of organic molecules including aromatic heterocycles, carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids, coenzymes, lipids, polymers, and their mechanisms.

nodes.title: Biochemistry
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 107A-B-C or 109A or 109AH-109B or 109BH-109C or 109CH or W 109C
nodes.description: Macromolecules of biological importance. A survey of the physical and chemical properties of proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates. Methods of preparation, chemical synthesis, degradation, and characterization of biomolecules.

nodes.title: Signal Analysis and Processing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 5A with a minimum of grade of C; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to EE and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Analysis of continuous time linear systems in the time and frequency domains. Superposition and convolution. Bilateral and unilateral Laplace transforms. Fourier series and Fourier transforms. Filtering, modulation, and feedback.

nodes.title: Signal Analysis and Processing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 130A with a minimum grade of C- or better; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to EE and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Analysis of discrete time linear systems in the time and frequency domains. Z transforms, Discrete Fourier transforms. Sampling and aliasing.

nodes.title: Introduction to Applied Linear Algebra
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Math 4B or Math 5A recommended. Open to EE and CE majors only.

items.text: Open to EE and CE majors only

nodes.description: Introduction to applied linear algebra: matrix arithmetic, vector spaces, orthogonality, matrix factorizations, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, difference and differential equations.

nodes.title: Introductory Biology II--Ecology and Evolution
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to population and community ecology, and evolution.

nodes.title: Introductory Biology III
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-B and EEMB 2 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the major groups of microbes, plants, and animals.

nodes.title: Introductory Genetics
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and EEMB 3 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to genetics. Mendel's laws, structure, replication and expression of DNA, linkage and chromosomal aberrations, mutation and recombination, concepts of genetic variability, quantitative and populationgenetics.

nodes.title: Introduction to Programming
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.description: General philosophy of programming and problem-solving. Students will be introduced to the programming language MATLAB. Specific areas of study will include algorithms, basic decision structures, arrays, matrices, and graphing.

nodes.title: Ethics in Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Senior standing in engineering.
nodes.description: The nature of moral value, normative judgment and moral reasoning. Theories of moral value. The engineer's role in society. Ethics in professional practice. Safety, risk, responsibility. Morality and career choice. Code of ethics. Case studies facilitate the comprehension of the concepts introduced.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement

nodes.title: Quantitative Thinking in Environmental Studies
nodes.description: Designed to improve students' ability to quantitatively approach environmental topics by developing skills in algebra, statistics, and calculus. Emphasis is placed on applying these skills to solve practical environmental problems. Students learn how to use widely used software for environmental data analysis and visualization (Excel and R, optionally). Designed for first and second year students to prepare them for upper division courses with quantitative components.

nodes.title: Renewable Energy Systems
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; Mathematics 2B, or 3B, or 34B, or Mathematics 34A and Environmental Studies 25.
nodes.description: Introduction to renewable energy generation and energy storage technologies, their economics, their associated environmental and social issues, and policies and regulations important to the adoption and use of renewable energy systems. Course includes field trips and guest lecturers.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Math 3A with precalculus: A function approach integrating algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus. Topics include: one-on-one and onto functions; inverse functions; properties and graphs of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; properties and graphs of trigonometric functions; analytic geometry; functions and limits; derivatives; techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Math 3B with precalculus: A continued review of relevant topics from precalculus (see Math 2A); integral calculus, including definite and indefinite integrals; techniques of integration, introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, First Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Differential Calculus including analytic geometry, functions and limits, derivatives, techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Integral calculus including definite and indefinite integrals, techniques of integration; introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra with Applications
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces and subspaces, basis and dimension, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, and orthogonality.

groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR

nodes.title: Differential Equations
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: First and second order differential equations, separation of variables, linear differential equations, systems of first order equations, nonlinear differential equations and stability.

groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR

nodes.title: Vector Calculus with Applications, First Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A (or 4AI) with a letter grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Calculus of functions of several variables, vector valued functions of one variable, derivative and integrals of vector functions, double and triple integrals, properties and applications of integrals, change of variables.

nodes.title: Vector calculus with Applications, Second Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B (or 4BI) and Mathematics 6A, each with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Scalar and vector fields, integration along paths, integration over surfaces and solid regions, integral theorems of vector calculus, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

nodes.title: Transition to Higher Mathematics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the elements of propositional logic, techniques of mathematical proof, and fundamental mathematical structures, including sets, functions, relations, and other topics as time permits. Mastery of this material is essential for students planning to major in mathematics.

nodes.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
nodes.description: Introduction to differential and integral calculus with applications to modeling in the biological sciences.

nodes.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A or 34LA with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Continued study of differential and integral calculus with differential andintegral calculus with applications. Introduction to mathematical modeling with differential equations. Calculus of several variables including an introduction to partial derivatives.

nodes.title: Calculus for the Life Sciences
nodes.description: Applications of differential and integral calculus to the life sciences. Includes mathematical foundations, biology examples, and computer programming to simulate dynamic systems.

nodes.title: Theory of Complex Variables
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Math 6A and 8 each with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Complex numbers, complex differentiation, analytic functions, Cauchy-Riemann equations, Taylor and Laurent series, classification of singular points, residues, evaluation of improper integrals.

nodes.title: Theory of Complex Variables
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Math 122A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: The argument principle, Rouche’s theorem, analytic continuation, conformal mapping, fractional transformations and applications, infinite products, harmonic functions. Other topics at the discretion of the instructor.

nodes.title: Structure and Properties I
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B and Mathematics 4B, 6A, 6B
nodes.description: An introduction to materials in modern technology. The internal structure of materials and its underlying principles: bonding, spatial organization of atoms and molecules, structural defects. Electricial, magnetic and optical properties of materials, and their relationship with structure.

nodes.title: Structures and Properties II
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Materials 100A.
nodes.description: Mechanical properties of engineering materials and their relationship to bonding and structure. Elastic, flow, and fracture behavior; time dependent deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms. Thermo-mechanical interactions in materials.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Structural Evolution
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Materials 100A and Materials 100B.
nodes.description: An introduction to the thermodynamic and kinetic principles governing structural evolution in materials. Phase equilibria, diffusion and structural transformations. Metastable structures in materials. Self-assembling systems. Structural control through processing and/ or imposed fields. Environmental effects on structure and properties.

nodes.title: Introduction to the Structure and Properties of Materials
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.description: Introduction to the structure of engineering materials and its relationship with their mechanical properties. Structure of solids and defects. Concepts of microstructure and origins. Elastic, plastic flow and fracture properties. Mechanisms of deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms.

nodes.title: Biophysics and Biomolecular Materials
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 6C or 25.
nodes.description: Structure and function of cellular molecules (lipids, nucleic acids, proteins, and carbohydrates). Genetic engineering techniques of molecular biology. Biomolecular materials and biomedical applications (e.g., bio-sensors, drug delivery systems, gene carrier systems).

nodes.title: Introduction to Polymer Science
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Chemical Engineering 110A or Chemistry 113A or equivalent.
nodes.description: Introductory course covering synthesis, characterization, structure, and mechanical properties of polymers. The course is taught from a materials perspective and includes polymer thermodynamics, chain architecture, measurement and control of molecular weight as well as crystallization and glass transitions.

nodes.title: Materials in Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Materials 100B or 101.
nodes.description: Introduces the student to the main families of materials and the principlesbehind their development, selection, and behavior. Discusses the generic properties of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites more relevant to structural applications. The relationship of properties to structure and processing is emphasized in every case.

nodes.title: Introductory Biology I
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B-C with a grade of C- or better (Chem 1C may be taken concurrently), or a score of 4 or better on either the Advanced Placement Chemistry or Advanced Placement Biology exams.

items.text: a score of 4 or better on either the Advanced Placement Chemistry or Advanced Placement Biology exams

nodes.description: Introduction to biochemistry, cell biology and development, and genetics.

nodes.title: Introductory Biology II--Physiology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A and Chemistry 1A-B-C with a grade of C- or better; or MCDB 1A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to animal and plant physiology.

nodes.title: Molecular Genetics I: Prokaryotes
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A-B, EEMB 2; and, Chemistry 1A-B-C; completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: From the double helix and genetic code to the latest breakthroughs. Structure, function, evolution and manipulation of DNA, RNA. Replication, expression, recombination, complementation, and their regulation in prokaryotes (bacteria, plasmids, viruses). Recombinant DNA technology in medicine, research, agriculture and industry.

nodes.title: Molecular Genetics II: Eukaryotes
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B, and MCDB 101A. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Mendelian and molecular genetics. Replication, recombination, transmission and expression of DNA in eukaryotic organisms from yeast to man. Uses of traditional genetics and modern molecular techniques, including molecular genetic approaches to the study of human disease.

nodes.title: Biochemistry - Structure and Function of Macromolecules
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and Chemistry 1A-B-C; and Chemistry 109A-B-C (Chem 109C may be taken concurrently). Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the structures and functions of proteins, including enzymes, with emphasis on their basic architecture and biological mechanisms of action and regulation. Methods used for characterizing proteins and analyzing enzyme kinetic data are also emphasized.

nodes.title: Biochemistry - Bioenergetics, Enzymology, and Metabolism
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 108A or MCDB W 108A with a grade of C or better.Chem 109C with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Principles of human energy metabolism. Chemistry and physiology of the major metabolic pathways of energy production. Metabolic interrelationships of the major body organs. Applications to human nutrition and disease, exercise, starvation, obesity, and atherosclerosis.

nodes.title: Biochemistry - Computational & Systems Biology
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 108A-B with a grade of C or better or MCDB W 108A and MCDB 108B with a grade of C or better; Physics 6A-B-C with minimum grade of C (Physics 6C may be taken concurrently); Math 34A-B with a grade of C or better or Math 3A-B with a grade of C or better or Math 2A-B with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Models of Biochemical and Cellular Systems. Introductory systems-biology approach to model the design and the function of biological systems. Students will develop an intuition about physical concepts that are fundamental to discuss how biological organisms acquire and process information from the environment. Those concepts and tools will cover probabilities and basic dynamical systems theory. Students will build models of processes of increasing complexity, ranging from viral dynamics, bacterial resistance to drugs, the maintenance of homeostatic equilibrium (trp operon), biological oscillators (mitotic clock) and genetic switches underlying cellular decisions (bacteriophage lambda and lac operon).

nodes.title: Human Physiology
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Fundamentals of human physiology at the molecular, cellular and organismal levels. Emphasis on homeostatic mechanisms regulating intercellular communication, muscle function, circulation, metabolism and body fluid balance/composition.

nodes.title: Basic Pharmacology
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A (may be taken concurrently) or Chemistry 142C; Chemistry 109A-B-C. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Covers a wide range of drugs with a focus on drugs used to treat disorders of the nervous and cardiovascular systems, antibacterial agents, antivirals, and anticancer drugs. Also looks at the pharmacology of inflammation and coagulation. The goal is to understand the underlying physiology behind disorders of these systems and the mechanisms of the drugs used to treat them. Additional out-of-class hours are necessary.

nodes.title: Basic Pharmacology
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A or Chemistry 142C; Chemistry 109A-B-C. Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Receptor signaling mechanisms; pharmacology of neurotransmitter and hormone receptors; molecular and cellular mechanisms of drug-receptor interactions.

nodes.title: Molecular and Cellular Immunobiology
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the current concepts of immunology. Emphasis on immunoglobulin structure and function, cell-cell cooperation in the immune response, and the role of major histocompatibility complex and cytokines in regulating immune responsiveness.

nodes.title: Medical Immunology
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 101A OR EEMB 129 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: By focusing on recent groundbreaking advances in our understanding of the vertebrate immune system, this course explores the contrasting mechanisms of protective immunity against parasites and cancer with various immune disorders that mainly stem from immune dysregulation, such as autoimmunity, acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), allergies, and other diseases. By engaging in interactive, case-based computer exercises, students will have an opportunity to emulate the discovery of the underlying biological defects that give rise to these and other immune-related diseases.

nodes.title: Biochemistry - Structure and Function of Macromolecules
nodes.prereq_text: MCDB 1A, and EEMB 2 and MCDB 1B; and Chemistry 1A-B-C; and Chemistry 109A-B-C (Chem 109C may be taken concurrently). Completion of all listed prerequisites with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the structures and functions of proteins, including enzymes, with emphasis on their basic architecture and biological mechanisms of action and regulation. Methods used for characterizing proteins and analyzing enzyme kinetic data are also emphasized.

nodes.title: Engineering Graphics: Sketching, CAD and Conceptual Design
nodes.prereq_text: Mechanical Engineering majors only.
nodes.description: Introduces hands-on engineering design via lessons on the design process, Computer Aided Design (CAD), free hand sketching, use of a laser cutter, soldering, basic circuits, basic microprocessor programming, motors and gear trains. Makes use of a robotic project to allow students to practice all above topics. Students create dimensioned engineering drawings and present their designs at a final design fair. The focus of the course is to empower students to leverage all engineering tools listed above in their future engineering courses.

nodes.title: Statics
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B, or Math 3B, or AP Calculus AB with a score of 5, or AP Calculus BC with a score of 3 or better; and Physics 7A, or Physics 1

items.text: AP Calculus AB with a score of 5

nodes.description: Introduction to applied mechanics. Forces, moments, couples, and resultants; vector algebra; construction of free body diagrams; equilibrium in 2- and 3-dimensions; analysis of frames, machines, trusses and beams; distributed forces; friction.

nodes.title: Strength of Materials
nodes.prereq_text: ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-; open to mechanical engineering majors only.

items.text: open to mechanical engineering majors only

nodes.description: Properties of structural materials, including Hookes law and behavior beyond the elastic limit. Concepts of stress, strain, displacement, force, force systems, and multiaxial stress states. Design applications to engineering structures, including problems of bars in tension, compression, and torsion, beams subject to flexure, pressure vessels, and buckling.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C (may be taken concurrently); open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Vectorial kinematics of particles. Coordinate systems, moving frames, relative and constrained motion. Dynamics of particles and systems of particles. Energy and momentum methods. Collisions. Planar kinematics and kinematics of rigid bodies. Energy and momentum methods for rigid body systems.

nodes.title: Dynamical Systems
nodes.prereq_text: Math 6B and ME 16
nodes.description: Equations of Motion for Mechanical, Electrical, Heat, Fluid, and Control Systems. Block diagram algebra and interconnections. Laplace transform. Transfer functions and dynamic stability. First and second order systems. Frequency response. Introduction to mechanical vibrations and feedback control design.

nodes.title: Aerodynamics and Aeronautical Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Mechanical Engineering 14 and 152A
nodes.description: Concepts from aerodynamics, including lift and drag analysis for airfoils as well as aircraft sizing/scaling issues. Structural mechanics concepts are applied to practical aircraft design. Intended for students considering a career in aeronautical engineering.

nodes.title: Energy
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Senior Undergraduate or Graduate Student status in the College of Engineering; or consent of Instructor
nodes.description: Introduction to the field of Energetics. Topics may include energy sources and production, energy usage, renewable technologies, hardware, operating principles, environmental impact, energy reserves, national and global energy budgets, historical perspectives, economics, societal considerations, and others.

nodes.title: Design of Biomedical Devices
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Mechanical Engineering 10, 14, 15, 16 or ME W 16, and 153; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Introductory course addresses the challenges of biomedical device design, prototyping and testing, material considerations, regulatory requirements, design control, human factors and ethics.

nodes.title: Projects in Thermal Sciences
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of Instructor
nodes.description: The focus of the class is on Heat Transfer, Energetics, and Fluid Mechanics. The primary activity will be individual projects on topics selected by each student in associated areas such as Alternative Energy technologies, Manufacturing, HVAC, Engines, Electronic devices, etc. Topics may be related to Senior Capstone projects, professional work, Research, Engineering competitions or clubs, internships, etc. Intended for Juniors, Seniors, and Graduate students in Engineering and the Physics department, with enrollment subject to Instructor approval.

nodes.title: Fluid Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Math 6B or Math 5C, and ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-, and Physics 7B or Physics 2
nodes.description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts in fluid mechanics and basic fluid properties. Basic equations of fluid flow. Dimensional analysis and similitude. Hydrodynamics.

nodes.title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering Design
nodes.prereq_text: ME 10 and 16 or ME W 16; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: This course introduces engineering design with a focus on an iterative design process. Throughout the course, a group project cements the topics learned through active application to a real design problem. The lectures are broken into three sections. Section 1 introduces a version of this iterative Design Cycle, which comprises four components: 1) Define, 2) Ideate, 3) Prototype & Test, and 4) Analyze. These steps are repeated many times over the course of design development, not always in this order. Section 2 of the course focuses on applying this Design Cycle to the team project. Section 3 wraps up and focuses on presenting the project.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Vibrations
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-; ME 103; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Topics relating to vibration in mechanical systems; exact and approximate methods of analysis, matrix methods, generalized coordinates and Lagrange's equations, applications of systems. Basic feedback systems and controlled dynamic behavior.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Phenomena
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 105A or Physics 103; or ME 163 or upper-division standing in ECE.
nodes.description: Introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Flows and bifurcations in one and two dimensions, chaos, fractals, strange attractors. Applications to physics, engineering, chemistry, and biology.

nodes.title: Materials in Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Materials 100B or 101.
nodes.description: Introduces the main families of materials and the principles behind their development, selection, and behavior. Discusses the generic properties of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites more relevant to structural applications. The relationship of properties to structure and processing is emphasized in every case.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C (may be taken concurrently); open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Vectorial kinematics of particles. Coordinate systems, moving frames, relative and constrained motion. Dynamics of particles and systems of particles. Energy and momentum methods. Collisions. Planar kinematics and kinematics of rigid bodies. Energy and momentum methods for rigid body systems.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Introduction to classical mechanics for students in engineering and the physical sciences. Measurement, units, and foundations of physics; vectors; kinematics; circular motion; forces, mass, and Newton's laws; center of mass; momentum; work and energy; conservation laws; collisions; rotational kinematics.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 1 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Rotational dynamics and angular momentum; equilibrium and elasticity; periodic motion including LRC electrical circuits; gravitation; fluid mechanics; temperature; thermal expansion; heat and the first law of thermodynamics; heat conduction; kinetic theory of gases; entropy and the second law; heat engines.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 2 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B (AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better) and 4A.

items.text: AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Mechanical waves, wave interference and normal modes, sound and hearing, electric field, Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.

nodes.title: Physics Laboratory
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 3 or 23 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introductory laboratory emphasizing periodic motion, sound and basic electronics.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 3 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.

nodes.title: Physics Laboratory
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 4 or 24 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introductory laboratory emphasizing magnetism, circuits and optics.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 4 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Special relativity, blackbody radiation, Compton scattering, photoelectric effect, Bohr model, quantum mechanics, molecules, condensed matter, nuclear physics, elementary particles.

nodes.title: Introductory Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A (may be taken concurrently) or AP Math AB Exam score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Vectors, velocity, acceleration. Newton's laws. Work and energy. Linear momentum. Gravity. Static equilibrium. Rotational motion. Angular momentum.

nodes.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Physics 6A.
nodes.description: Self directed laboratory course where students seek to discover simple mathematical descriptions of laws governing various physical phenomena. Each student is responsible for deciding what to measure, how to measure it, and what interpretation can be placed on the results.

nodes.title: Introductory Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 6A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Oscillatory motion. Vibrations, waves, sound. Fluids. Electrostatics and DC circuits. Magnetism and magnetic forces. Induction and Faraday's law. AC circuits. If time permits: Heat and thermodynamics.

nodes.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Physics 6B.
nodes.description: Experiments in the mechanical, electrical and thermal properties of matter,the behavior of light, and quantum phenomena with application to the biological sciences.

nodes.title: Introductory Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 6B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Electromagnetic waves. Geometric optics, optical instruments. Interference and diffraction. Quantum theory of the atom. Nuclear physics. If time permits: Special relativity, elementary particle physics.

nodes.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in Physics 6C.
nodes.description: Experiments in the mechanical, electrical and thermal properties of matter,the behavior of light, and quantum phenomena with application to the biological sciences.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Kinematics in 3D, Newton’s Laws, Energy, Momentum and Collisions, Rotation, Statics and Equilibrium

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Gravity, Periodic Motion and Oscillations, Mechanical Waves and Sound, Coulomb’s Law, Electric Field and Gauss’s Law, Electric Potential, DC circuits

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7B with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Magnetic Forces and Field, Induction, Inductance and AC circuits, Maxwell’s equations and E/M waves, Geometric and Physical Optics

nodes.title: Physics Laboratory
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7B; Co-requisite: Physics 7C
nodes.description: Periodic motion, sound, and basic electronics, while emphasizing good laboratory techniques such as uncertainty propagation, statistical analysis, developing and testing models, and good report writing.

nodes.title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods for Physics
nodes.description: Single variable functions, derivatives and integrals with applications to kinematics. Taylor series. Introduction to ordinary differential equations and Newtons second law as an ODE. Vectors and scalars with physics applications. Dot and cross products. Matrices and determinants. Unit circle and trigonometric identities. Polar coordinates and kinematics in polar coordinates.

nodes.title: Honors Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Design and construction of apparatus, drafting and computer-aided design. Machine shop practice including use of all major machine tools. The class acts as a team to design and, time permitting, build a scientific apparatus for a campus research group.

nodes.title: Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 29 and Physics 23 (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation. Basic good practices in note-taking, data collection, data visualization, error estimation, error propagation, curve fitting, and drawing conclusions, all exercised in the context of phenomena from mechanics and electronics.

nodes.title: Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 20AL and Physics 24 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, continued. Basics of image analysis, technical drawing, additive manufacturing, oscilloscope use, searching and digesting scientific literature, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL in the context of electromagnetic and optical phenomena.

nodes.title: Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 20BL and Physics 25 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, with an emphasis on Scientific Communication and Experimental Design. Searching the scientific literature, reading a scientific paper, proposing and executing a measurement, and formally reporting on a measurement in writing, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL and 20BL in the context of modern physics phenomena.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A/3A and Mathematics 2B/3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam score of 5.
nodes.description: Classical mechanics, kinematics, vectors, Newtons laws, work and energy, conservation laws, rotational kinematics.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 21 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Rotational dynamics, fluid mechanics, gravitation, periodic motion, temperature and heat, thermodynamics.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 22 with a minimum grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Mechanical waves, sound, electric charge and electric field, Gauss Law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 23 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4A.
nodes.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 24 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 6A.
nodes.description: Special relativity, blackbody radiation, Compton scattering, photoelectric effect, Bohr model, quantum mechanics, molecules, condensed matter, nuclear physics, elementary particles.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Programming for the Physical Sciences
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2B or 3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam with a score of 5

items.text: AP Calculus BC Exam with a score of 5

nodes.description: An introduction to programming and data analysis for the physical sciences. Topics include syntax, goodcoding practice, basic algorithmic structure, plotting, basic data analysis, numerical root-finding and integration.

nodes.title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Linear Algebra: Vector spaces, operators, spectral decomposition. Topics may include Sturm-Liouville equations, special functions. Fourier series and Fourier transforms, Dirac delta-function.

nodes.title: Intermediate Mechanics and Special Relativity
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 2 or 22 with a minimum grade of C-. Mathematics 6A (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Newtonian mechanics in 3D. Conservation laws. Complex numbers. Oscillations. Inertial reference frames, Lorentz transformations, relativistic momentum and energy, four-vectors.

nodes.title: Quantum Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 and Physics 100A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: The postulates of quantum mechanics, the Schrdinger equation and its consequences, the quantum harmonic oscillator and other one dimensional quantum systems, Hilbert Space and Dirac notation, the hydrogen atom.

nodes.title: Quantum Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 115A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Spin and angular momentum, Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, identical particles, symmetries and conservation laws, time independent perturbation theory.

nodes.title: Condensed Matter Physics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 115A with at least a C- or better, and upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Classification of solids; crystal symmetry; thermal, electronic, and magnetic properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators; band theory of electronic states; wave scattering by crystals; semiconductor devices.

nodes.title: Condensed Matter Physics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 115B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Tight binding model, topological insulator, magnetism, phase transition, introduction to superconductivity.

nodes.title: Analog Electronics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 13CL or 20CL and Math 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Passive circuits, diodes, transistors, field effect transistors, operational amplifiers, feedback and control. Design, building and testing of analog circuits.

nodes.title: Digital Electronics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Technical Elective requirement
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 127AL with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Gates, combinational and sequential logic, ?multiplexers, counters, shift registers, memory and microprocessors. Design, building and testing of digital circuitry, including a modern microprocessor based computer system.
